## Added

- **Kimi Code** is now a provider. It shows your plan name and your 5-hour, weekly and monthly limits with their reset times, using the account you're signed in to with the `kimi` CLI. Turn it on under **Settings → Providers → Kimi Code**; first-run setup suggests it when Kimi Code is installed. The tab also shows Kimi Code's service status from Moonshot AI's status page.

Kimi Code's sign-in lasts about 15 minutes and Kimi Code only renews it while it's working. So that usage keeps updating when Kimi Code isn't running, UsageDeck renews the sign-in itself and saves it back for Kimi Code, as a second Kimi Code window would. If UsageDeck ever says it couldn't save a renewed sign-in, or Kimi Code asks you to sign in, run `kimi login`. Kimi Code sign-ins kept in the system keyring aren't supported yet.
